# Deferred native termination

This is the exact crates.io `i-slint-backend-winit` 1.18.1 source, with the narrow patch in [auditorylab.patch](auditorylab.patch). [auditorylab-provenance.json](auditorylab-provenance.json) records the upstream crate checksum, Git identity, and every original file hash. The Cargo registry download marker `.cargo-ok` is omitted. All upstream license files and notices are retained.

The selected Slint Royalty-free Desktop, Mobile, and Web Applications License 2.0 grants modification and distribution integrated into an Application (sections 1 and 2). This dependency is integrated into Auditory Lab; the selected grant does not authorize standalone redistribution of Slint (section 3). Auditory Lab retains the required Slint attribution in its About interface and distributes the full selected terms. This record adds no alternative license grant.

On macOS, Winit 0.30.13's default Quit menu and Dock Quit invoke AppKit termination. Its application delegate receives `applicationWillTerminate:` and directly closes native windows, bypassing `windowShouldClose:` and therefore the application's cancellation and join contract. Replacing the delegate is unsupported by this pinned Winit implementation. Slint already injects a native delegate selector for shortcut localization, so this patch uses the same narrow integration boundary instead of adding native FFI or a backend API to the application.

The injected `applicationShouldTerminate:` returns an NSUInteger `NSTerminateCancel` after delivering `windowShouldClose:` to a retained snapshot of Winit-managed window delegates. This selector follows the same CloseRequested route as the window close button. Direct delegate delivery avoids `performClose:`'s alert sound when Winit vetoes immediate closure, and excludes native file chooser panels. No controller or window registry borrow is held. Winit dispatches immediately when its event handler is free, and otherwise defers the close event, preserving its reentrancy guard. Repeated requests remain normal close requests; the controller owns idempotence. The application subsequently leaves its event loop only after its worker has settled and joined and any pending dialog has settled.

With no Winit-managed window the callback permits immediate termination. Auditory Lab creates and shows its main native window before starting any worker, and retains it through worker completion and join. A hidden retained main window still counts. This fallback is therefore for no remaining managed application lifetime, not a shortcut around a running operation. Missing or conflicting critical delegate selectors fail backend startup visibly rather than silently restoring the bypass.

This behavior qualifies ordinary macOS Quit, not force termination. Returning Cancel can cancel an operating-system logout/shutdown request; system logout negotiation is not qualified. NSTerminateLater was rejected because AppKit enters a modal run-loop mode while this Winit version defers queued application handlers to the default mode, risking a stranded cancellation/join path.

`AUDITORY_GUI_TERMINATION_TEST=1 cargo test -p auditory-gui --test native_termination --locked` runs a nonshipping native window fixture using an external safe Swift `NSRunningApplication.terminate()` helper. It tests idle, blocked-worker, repeated-Quit, and modeled pending-dialog holds, proving native CloseRequested delivery and window retention until actual thread join and event-loop return. It never opens audio. The dialog case models the controller hold; it does not open or automatically dismiss an actual native chooser. Production controller unit tests and native chooser checks supply separate evidence. Ordinary tests skip this display-dependent fixture explicitly.

The Wayland CSD feature selects Winit's crossfont alternative, retaining title rendering and controls while avoiding the unmaintained ttf-parser route. Its SCTK manifest-only crossfont update is reviewed separately; supported Linux builds require root Cargo system-FreeType overrides and updated distribution packages.
